title: Initial 3D Cell Cluster Control in a Hybrid Gel Cube Device for Repeatable Pattern Formations
protocol: Prepare a polycarbonate cubic frame using a machining process or a 3D printer.
Place the PC frame on a pre-cooled glass slide in an ice box.
Add 12 µL of pre-heated 1.5% agarose to the top face of the cubic frame and spread it to create a flat surface.
Allow the agarose to cure for several minutes.
Pick up the PC frame by sliding it to the edge of the glass slide using tweezers.
Rotate the cubic frame to make the open face down, and place it on the glass slide again.
Repeat steps 1.3–1.5 until three surfaces are filled with agarose.
Drop the agarose in from an open face to form an agarose wall on the fourth face.
Drop the agarose in from the fourth face to form an agarose wall on the fifth face, completing the HGC preparation.
Clean a silicon (Si) wafer via ultrasonic cleaning with acetone.
Clean the Si wafer via ultrasonic cleaning with isopropyl alcohol (IPA).
Clean the Si wafer via ultrasonic cleaning with distilled (DI) water.
Blow the Si wafer dry with nitrogen.
Dehydrate the Si wafer in an oven at 140 °C for 20 min.
Spin-coat a sacrificial layer such as LOR and Az resists on the Si wafer using a spin-coater under yellow light (2,000 rpm, 30 s).
Heat the wafer on a hot plate at 90 °C for 3 min after spin-coating.
Place the wafer on a hot plate at 70 °C.
Laminate a thick negative photoresist sheet with the desired thickness on the sacrificial layer using a hand roller.
Expose the wafer to UV light through a photomask with the desired pattern.
Post-exposure bake the wafer at 60 °C for 5 min.
Bake the wafer at 90 °C for 10 min after post-exposure baking.
Develop a negative photoresist by immersing the wafer in propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate (PGMEA) until the unexposed area is completely dissolved (approximately 20 min).
Dissolve the sacrificial layer using IPA for ultrasonic cleaning.
Lift off the microstructure from the wafer during the cleaning process.
Rinse the peeled-off microstructure with DI water through ultrasonic cleaning for 10 minutes.
Immerse the mold in 30 µL of MPC polymer at room temperature (approximately 20 °C) for 30 minutes to dry completely.
Fabricate a steel cylinder mold with desired dimensions by machining or using commercially available stainless steel.
Immerse the fabricated steel cylinder mold in 30 µL of MPC polymer at room temperature (approximately 20 °C) for 30 minutes to dry completely.
Mix liquid polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) base resin and its catalyst in a 10:1 ratio followed by degassing with a vacuum degassing system for 20 minutes.
Pour the prepared PDMS into a 12-well plate.
Insert the steel cylinder mold perpendicularly into the uncured PDMS surface on the 12-well plate using a linear z-stage.
Incubate the PDMS and steel cylinder mold in an oven at 90 °C for 20 minutes to cure.
Cut the cured PDMS to form a flank surface, allowing pipet insertion in subsequent processes.
Inject an appropriate ECM into the HGC to fill the culture space.
Set the fabricated micromold on the HGC directly or indirectly with an appropriate holder.
Place the HGC in a CO2 incubator for 25 min at 37 °C for curing it.
Carefully lift out the micromold so that the ECM does not deteriorate.
Harvest cells from the cultured dish by trypsin-EDTA or its equivalent depending on the cell types.
Centrifuge the cells to obtain highly concentrated cells.
Remove the supernatant medium to condense the cells.
Inject highly concentrated cells into the pocket in the ECM.
Incubate the HGC with cells in a CO2 incubator for 20 min at 37 °C.
If excessive medium or cells are present on the top surface, carefully remove using a pipette.
Place the HGC on a 24-well-plate and add 100 µL of appropriate medium.
Inject additional ECM to close the pocket in the ECM.
Incubate at 37 °C for 25 min.
Cool down preheated 1.5% agarose to room temperature (approximately 20 °C).
Drop approximately 10 µL of the agarose onto the top surface of the HGC to close the surface and prevent the ECM from falling out during culturing and imaging.
Incubate the HGC for another 20 min at 37 °C to cure the agarose.
Add medium to cover the entire HGC so that the osmotic pressure can help in providing nutrition to the cells inside the HGC.
Place the culture dish or well plate containing the HGC on a microscope and orient the HGC to the camera frame.
Obtain a sample image by bright field or phase contrast.
Pick up and rotate the HGC to place a different surface down.
Repeat steps until images from all six sides are obtained.
Apply 4% paraformaldehyde to the sample over the HGC at room temperature (approximately 20 °C) for 20 min, followed by two rinses of PBS for 10 min each.
Permeabilize the HGC with PBS containing 0.5% Triton X-100 for 10 min at 4 °C.
Wash the HGC 3x for 10 min with PBS.
Incubate the HGC with 10% goat serum in IF-buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 0.1% bovine serum albumin, and 0.05% Tween-20 in PBS) for 60 min at room temperature for a primary blocking step.
Use the appropriate antibody for staining a specific molecule.
Stain actin using Alexa Fluor 488 Phalloidin to observe collective cell geometry.
Place the HGC on a glass bottom dish under a laser or fluorescent microscope.
Perform scanning from six sides to obtain the entire sample image.
